# DNA replication

## Copying DNA

DNA replication produces two identical copies of a DNA molecule before a cell divides. The enzyme helicase unwinds the double helix and separates the two strands. Each separated strand then serves as a template for a new strand. DNA polymerase builds the new strand by adding nucleotides that pair with the template. Polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3 prime end of a growing strand.

## Accuracy

DNA polymerase also proofreads its work and removes most mismatched nucleotides. Replication is called semiconservative because each new molecule keeps one original strand. Errors that escape proofreading can become mutations.
